final_recommendation: The room converged on a base-case trilateral deal by late September 2018 (65% probability), with Canada joining the U.S.-Mexico bilateral under pressure. Key compromises expected: Canada preserves Chapter 19, grants limited dairy access, and accepts a review-mechanism sunset compromise. Labor enforcement details remain the decisive downstream ratification risk.
minority_objections: 25% probability scenario: talks stall into Q4 2018 if Canada refuses sufficient dairy concessions or Chapter 19 elimination remains a U.S. hard demand
10% probability: U.S.-Mexico bilateral only if catastrophic breakdown on Chapter 19 or dairy
key_conflicts: Chapter 19 dispute settlement: U.S. elimination objective vs. Canada's existential red line
Canadian dairy market access: U.S. dairy lobby demands vs. Canadian supply management political toxicity
Sunset clause: U.S. leverage retention vs. business community investment certainty needs
Labor enforcement specificity: U.S. labor union demands for facility-level enforcement vs. Mexican sovereignty concerns
key_concessions: U.S. expected to back down on Chapter 19 elimination (preservation with face-saving procedural modifications)
Canada expected to grant limited dairy market access via new TRQs (painful but survivable)
Sunset clause compromise: long base term (12-16 years) with periodic mandatory reviews instead of automatic termination
Canada accepts U.S.-Mexico auto rules framework (75% RVC, labor-value content) with little choice
red_lines: Canada: complete supply management dismantlement = no deal
Canada: hard sunset clause = no deal
U.S.: must have dairy concession sufficient to claim victory
U.S. labor unions: text-only labor commitments without enforcement = opposition
U.S. dairy lobby: deal without Canadian dairy concession = strong opposition from dairy-state senators
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: November 2018 midterm election impact on ratification timeline and Democratic House leverage was noted but the full implications of a 2019 ratification with new Congress may be underweighted
AMLO transition risk in Mexico (December 2018) and potential for incoming government to resist 'colonial' enforcement despite outgoing government commitments
Cumulative compliance costs across multiple new requirements (auto RVC + labor-value content + steel/aluminum) may exceed industry's stated concerns
downstream_risk_variables: Labor enforcement protocol details and timing (before vs. after signature)
AFL-CIO endorsement decision based on enforcement credibility
November 2018 midterm results determining House control and ratification dynamics
Dairy TRQ amounts and product coverage sufficiency for U.S. dairy lobby
Auto industry assessment of compliance costs and transition timeline adequacy
Democratic House demands for side letters or Protocol of Amendment in 2019
Mexican domestic ratification under AMLO government if enforcement seen as sovereignty violation
uncertainty_notes: Labor enforcement mechanism details remain unresolved and are identified as the highest ratification risk (60% probability of problems). The November 2018 midterm outcome will fundamentally reshape ratification dynamics. If Democrats win the House, the analysis projects 70% probability of demands for modifications to signed text. The exact structure of dairy TRQs and whether they satisfy U.S. dairy lobby remains uncertain. Auto industry's final assessment of compliance costs under 75% RVC + labor-value content is pending detailed implementation rules.
